Methodology: faffter-noon-methodology-thematic

## What's up: 2026-11-16

**7 days to Recovery beta**

### Milestones

Source of truth is the configured issue tracker. Snapshot below; re-query the tracker's milestones per project for the live view.

#### Account recovery

| Milestone | Target | Progress |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Recovery beta | 2026-11-23 | 50% |

### Shipped
- BRF-10  Records each account-recovery attempt. Unlocked: BRF-11 (issues the tokens a user needs to recover an account)

### In progress
- BRF-12  Adds the screen users see when recovering an account: Building

### Blocked
- BRF-13  Sends the account-recovery emails: blocked, waiting for BRF-11

### Parked overnight
- BRF-20  Chooses how long recovery data is kept: parked in interactive prep because the product retention decision remains open. Unpark: re-run `/faff-prep BRF-20` once it is decided (no run log; manual park)
- BRF-21  Repairs the importer: parked by an autonomous graft because schema compatibility is unclear. Unpark: re-run `/faff-graft BRF-21` (log: .faff/runs/run-a/BRF-21/graft.md)

### Awaiting review (adversarial outage)
- BRF-22  Stops duplicate recovery emails being sent: review provider unavailable, attempt 1/3; branch pushed. Auto-resumes on the next build drain without rebuilding, no action needed

### Awaiting spec-review (adversarial outage)
- BRF-23  Sets the scope of the token expiry policy: spec-review provider unavailable, held drain 2/4; spec attached. Auto-resumes on the next prep drain without re-spec, no action needed

### ADR supersession proposals awaiting ratification
- ADR-0042 (Use token ledger) proposes to supersede ADR-0031 (Use transient tokens), authored by BRF-12: need a durable retry record. Ratify supersession of ADR-0031 by ADR-0042? (y/n)

### Do this
Ordered by the methodology's pick-ordering.

1. BRF-11  Issues recovery tokens. Shipping it clears the last blocker on the recovery emails (BRF-13), which in turn opens up auditing recovery delivery (BRF-14). (Priority source: issue; just unlocked by BRF-10.)
2. BRF-12  Finish the recovery screen already in progress. (Priority source: issue.)

### Methodology findings

WIP at 1 (cap 3). Below cap: up to 2 new starts.

### Automation preview: fire `/faff-beep-boop`?

**Value chains to unlock**
  BRF-11  issue recovery tokens  →  unlocks BRF-13 → BRF-14  (2 issues; 1 blocked only by BRF-11, BRF-14 still gated by BRF-13)

**Build queue** (1 ready · 1 fire-and-forget · 0 collision groups)

  fire-and-forget
    BRF-11  Issue recovery tokens

**Needs your call before automation can pick up:**

  needs-decision-first
    (architecture)
      BRF-30  Picks where rate-limit counters are stored: Punt in spec: Redis or database?
    (product)
      BRF-31  Sets the account-recovery policy: Punt in spec: who can reset an account?
    (unowned)
      BRF-32  Chooses the replay window: confidence: medium (spec thin on retry timing); prep attached for review

  gap-blocked
    (none)

  circular-blocked
    (none)

  repeat-parked
    (none)

**Prep queue** (1 candidate, drained by default `/faff-beep-boop`)
- BRF-33  Records when a token is revoked: no spec

### Structural diagnostics

Structural diagnostics: clean ✓

### Ready to pick up
- BRF-11  Issue recovery tokens: spec ready (just unlocked by BRF-10) (unlocks 2)

Next steps:
- Picking up BRF-11? It has a spec. Start building now via `/faff-graft`? (y/n)
- BRF-20 parked: re-run `/faff-prep` / leave parked (reprep/leave)
- BRF-21 parked: open log / re-run `/faff-graft` / leave parked (log/reprep/leave)
